page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-96 is a memory-optimized server instance from the n4d family. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 architecture, paired with 768.0 GB of system memory. This configuration provides a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, designed for memory-intensive workloads that require substantial RAM capacity alongside high-core compute density.

This server type does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met through network-attached block storage options. Additionally, it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing performance without resource contention from other tenants, though the lack of local NVMe storage represents a tradeoff for I/O-heavy operations.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n4d-highmem-96 offers a high-density resource profile suitable for enterprise applications. The balance of 96 dedicated cores and 768.0 GB of RAM makes it appropriate for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems, enterprise resource planning applications, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
